text: Everything so far has been building the data. This lesson builds the two numbers leadership actually asked for in Lesson 1 -- Monthly Recurring Revenue and churn -- as real DAX measures over the marts.

fct_subscriptions is event-grained, one row per signup, upgrade, or cancel -- not one row per subscriber per month. A plain SUM would add up every event ever recorded, including cancellations. CALCULATE fixes that with two filters: only revenue-generating event types, and only subscribers whose cancelled_at is still blank, meaning they're currently active.
That measure lands on a Card visual -- the same real Power BI Desktop card-building flow Driftwood's MRR, churn-rate, and active-subscriber tiles all use.

Churn rate is a ratio, not a count. Subscribers Cancelled This Month counts cancellations since the start of the month; Active Subscribers Start of Month counts subscribers who'd already signed up and hadn't yet cancelled. DIVIDE, not a plain slash, returns blank instead of an error the first month there's no baseline yet.

Adding each visual to the canvas follows the same real Power BI workflow -- pick a visual type, drag the measure in, and it slices cleanly by month using the same time-intelligence patterns the Power BI course's DAX chapters already taught.

The executive dashboard itself is deliberately simple: three cards -- MRR, churn rate, active subscribers -- a twelve-month MRR trend line, and a churn-rate table. Leadership asked for one trustworthy number, not a feature-complete analytics tool.
Next lesson: securing subscriber PII with RBAC and masking, before this platform goes anywhere near production.
